source_name: BBC by Lana Lam, syndicated by AOL
summary:
Australia's online safety regulator has identified inconsistent safeguards across four popular gaming services: Steam, Roblox, Fortnite and Minecraft. The findings raise questions about how companies design and maintain spaces used by children.

According to research cited in the BBC's report, nine out of ten Australian children aged eight to seventeen have played online games. Gaming platforms can connect people through both games and communication features. The regulator therefore examined more than the games themselves: it looked at systems for finding harmful content, checking users' ages and sharing safety knowledge.

One issue was the difference between declaring an age and verifying it. If a service simply asks people how old they are, it may not know whether the answer is accurate. The report described age checks that varied between platforms, as well as differences in tools used to detect harmful material and in cooperation with other companies.

Its findings are tied to a particular time period. The information collected concerned protections in place from October 2025 through March 2026. The BBC also noted subsequent or recent changes, including stronger checks on Roblox and credit-card age checks on Steam. Readers should therefore avoid treating the report as a complete description of every platform's systems today.

Roblox said it prioritizes the safety of its Australian community and has invested heavily in safeguards, including mandatory age checks. The BBC said it had contacted the other companies for comment. A company's response is relevant context, but a statement of commitment is different from evidence that a particular safeguard works well.

Australia's earlier restriction on social-media accounts for people under sixteen did not include gaming platforms, the BBC reported. This review concerns gaming safety and should not be confused with an announcement that those games have been banned.

The central question is how companies can make protections more reliable and consistent. For young readers, the story is a reminder that the design of digital spaces is a public-policy issue. Responsibility for safe systems belongs to the organizations building and operating them.
title: Australian Report Finds Uneven Safeguards in Online Games
why_it_matters: Many young people use online games, making the quality of platform safeguards important.
